script.base: Books make Green Bay a 3.5-point home favorite in a 48.5 total, so the expected script is a competitive Lambeau game that Green Bay leads by about a score late, not a blowout and not a slog. Implied points are GB 26.0 and WAS 22.5, enough plays for volume. Washington sits exactly on the 3.5 dog throw-more line, so Jayden Daniels should keep throwing to primary target Deebo Samuel (10 targets, 77 yards, 80 air yards) while the run game stays a committee: Jacory Croskey-Merritt 10 carries, Daniels 8, Austin Ekeler 6, Jeremy McNichols 4. script.flip1: Green Bay scores early, leads by two scores, and salts the clock with Jacobs. Washington abandons the run, so Croskey-Merritt's carries fall well under 10 and Daniels funnels targets to Deebo, Zach Ertz (5 targets week 1) and Terry McLaurin (4 targets, 77 air yards). That flip helps a Croskey-Merritt rush-yards under and a Deebo receiving-yards over, and it is the favorite-runs-the-clock path in the GB -3.5 number.
script.flip2: Daniels' legs (8 carries, 71 yards in week 1) keep Washington tied or in front. Green Bay cannot just hand it to Jacobs late, both passing games stay live, and a Washington clock-control script can give Croskey-Merritt more than 10 carries plus another explosive. That flip kills the Croskey-Merritt under and can cut Deebo's target share if Washington is content to run. Both candidate legs are tagged script-dependent on this flip.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both lost. Croskey-Merritt cleared 82.5 because the 82 yards already came on only 10 carries, so one explosive beat Green Bay's 2.24 yards-per-carry reputation, or Parsons sat and Washington handed the committee back a clock-control game with 18 carries. Deebo stayed under 77.5 because McLaurin already had 77 air yards on 4 targets and Ertz had 5 targets, and once Parsons was active the 10-target role became 5 catches for 40 yards, or an uncharted corner shadowed him. The worse split is Parsons out: Washington runs, the under dies, and Deebo can still go over, which means the two legs were never a perfect one-story pair if the game-time tag flips. Lambeau wind and rain were not saved, so a 15-plus mph night could have killed Deebo's 80 air yards and helped the under for a reason we could not price. Inactives were not locked. The lines were stand-ins, so there may have been no price edge at all even if the read was right.
